concept.title: Firefox schema channels and validation
concept.shortdesc: The Firefox schema channel controls which policies and values BPM can validate and show as supported.

conbody.p: Choose the channel that matches the browser fleet: Firefox Release 153, Firefox ESR 153.0, Firefox ESR 140.13, or Firefox ESR 115.39. Schema choice changes available controls, validation messages, and whether a setting is supported, unavailable, deprecated, unknown, imported, or preserved as raw data.

section.title: Choose a channel
section.p: The supported schema channels are Release 153, ESR 153.0, ESR 140.13, and ESR 115.39. Select the channel before you import, validate, edit detailed settings, or export a profile. ESR 115.39 serves organizations with legacy systems through limited critical-security support; it does not make an unsupported operating system vendor-supported. Its reviewed support boundary is rechecked on 2027-03-01.

section.title: Validation
section.p: Validation checks the profile against the selected schema and BPM normalized model. Run validation before export, after JSON edits, after import, and before comparing important profiles.

section.title: Understand Release and ESR differences
section.p: Common policies such as DisableTelemetry validate in all four supported channels. Release 153 and ESR 153.0 can support newer controls such as AIControls and VisualSearchEnabled that are absent in ESR 140.13 and ESR 115.39.

section.title: Supported, unavailable, deprecated, unknown, and raw states
section.p: Supported settings can be edited and validated for the selected schema. Unavailable or unknown settings should be reviewed before handoff; deprecated settings may still exist but require current-channel confirmation; raw fallback values should be preserved or removed deliberately.

section.title: Review a channel change
section.p: Switching schema channels is a review decision, not a silent migration. For any distinct pair of the four current artifacts, choose the target and read the preview first. Preview is read-only: each source item is reported as unchanged, approvedly transformed, or blocked. Apply is available only after an applicable, target-valid preview with no blockers and an explicit confirmation; it atomically updates the saved profile. Revalidate after switching and inspect newer-channel, ESR-unavailable, imported, raw, or deprecated values before you save or export.

section.title: Review the support boundary
section.p: DisableTelemetry is a common valid example. AIControls and VisualSearchEnabled can be valid on Release 153 or ESR 153.0 and unsupported on ESR 140.13. Wrong value types, such as a string for DisableTelemetry, are invalid for every schema.

section.title: Recovery
section.p: If validation fails, read the affected policy path, confirm the schema channel, inspect the setting in All settings or JSON editor, and only then edit, remove, or preserve the value.
